citations.description: Ticket status is `in_progress`; ticket comments contain no CI run ID, log line, or timestamp attesting a passing `make lint`/`make typecheck`/`make test` run.

findings.criterion: `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL gating suite (`make test`, not just `tests/unit`) pass
findings.detail: This criterion requires CI execution results (lint, typecheck, full test suite) that are inherently outside the codebase. The ticket is still `in_progress` and no concrete attestation of a passing CI run (no run ID, no log line, no timestamp) appears in the ticket comments. The criterion is untagged (codebase-verifiable by default), but its evidence lives entirely outside the repository — it cannot be confirmed from file inspection alone. No operator-attested tag was applied, so it cannot be credited via attestation either.
findings.remediation: Record a concrete attestation in a ticket comment naming the CI run URL/ID, the observed outcome (all checks green), and the timestamp/SHA at which it passed. Tag the criterion `[operator-attested]` if the intent is for CI evidence to satisfy it.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
